ammonium sulfate nitrate.reason: Ammonium sulphate nitrate is a distinct double-salt nitrogen fertiliser that falls between the Ammonium Sulphate and Ammonium Nitrate labels, so neither is a clean match and no single allowed label fits well.

asaase wura.reason: This is a Twi phrase roughly meaning 'owner of the land' and is likely a Ghanaian trade name, but I cannot reliably tie it to a specific fertiliser type in the list.

chicken droppings.label: Organic Fertilizer
chicken droppings.reason: Chicken droppings are poultry manure, which is an organic fertiliser.

cocoa husk ash.label: Organic Fertilizer
cocoa husk ash.reason: Cocoa husk ash is a potassium-rich ash made from crop residue and used as a soil amendment, so it fits best as an organic or natural fertiliser rather than any synthetic mineral product.

liquid boost.label: Foliar Fertilizer
liquid boost.reason: A liquid booster product is most commonly a foliar-applied fertiliser, though the vague name could also describe a liquid organic or bio-stimulant product.

sulphan.label: Ammonium Nitrate
sulphan.reason: Sulphan is a Zimbabwean trade name for an ammonium sulphate nitrate top-dressing that is mostly ammonium nitrate with added sulphur, so it partly overlaps the ammonium sulphate label too.

yara mila actyva.label: NPK Compound
yara mila actyva.reason: YaraMila Actyva is a Yara branded compound granular fertiliser supplying nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium with secondary nutrients, so it fits the NPK compound category.
